main_text.p: cronibus audaciæ atq; virium ostentandarum gratiâ, populi Herod. Histor. l. 1. in vitâ Comm.explebant animum. Quarum adeo avidi fuere nonnulli Imperatores Romani, ut potius gladiatorum consortio interesse, atque ex eorum catogogio prodire mallent, quam cum senatoribus in senatu versari, ibique rempublicâ administrare.

Verum quidem est, videri talia spectacula quasi jure naturæ introducta, ut illud jus naturæ accipitur, pro aliquo instinctu naturæ, quo nascitur aliqua inclinatio; quæ virium corporalium inducit experientiam.

Attamen ut illa inclinatio ten-dit ulterius, ac se diffundit ad mutuam læsionem & vul-nera, in tantum non ea potest dici juris naturæ, ut ab eâ abhorreat ipsa natura. Talia igi-tur duellorum vel certami-num genera, de omni jure il-licita judicamus.

page.notes: The bullet-like mark beside the line "Attamen" and the small marks at the lower left are printer's marks or specks, not text, and are not transcribed. The grey strip at the lower right is a scan edge. The marginal note reads as one block spanning "Herod." to "Comm."; its exact line breaks are not certain. "Hiftor." is printed with long s and is given as "Histor.". "catogogio" is printed this way (probably for catalogio) and is left as printed.
